Committee: Tourism
Sponsor: Allen
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 03/17/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 333 as introduced would increase the obligations of the Alabama Athletic Commission by an undetermined amount to regulate unarmed combat. Any increase in obligations could be offset, wholly or in part, by: (1) license fees imposed for the promotion or holding of unarmed combat events and for participants of unarmed combat events; and (2) administrative fines the Commission is authorized, pursuant to the provisions of this bill, to assess and collect in an amount not to exceed $10,000 per violation.
Also, this bill as introduced could reduce potential receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; reduce receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could reduce the obligations of the State General Fund, local jails, the district attorneys, the Department of Corrections, the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles, and community corrections programs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons who would have otherwise been charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by current law and the penalties currently imposed.
Del Marsh, Chairperson
Tourism

Any increase in obligations could be offset, wholly or in part, by: (1) license fees imposed for the promotion or holding of unarmed combat events and for participants of unarmed combat events; and (2) administrative fines the Commission is authorized, pursuant to the provisions of this bill, to assess and collect in an amount not to exceed $10,000 per violation.
Also, this bill as introduced could reduce potential receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; reduce receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could reduce the obligations of the State General Fund, local jails, the district attorneys, the Department of Corrections, the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles, and community corrections programs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons who would have otherwise been charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by current law and the penalties currently imposed.
As amended and reported by the Committee on Tourism, removes the provision which made participation in, or promotion of, unarmed combat a Class A misdemeanor.
Del Marsh, Chairperson

Committee: Boards, Agencies and Commissions
Sponsor: Allen
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 04/12/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 333 as passed the Senate would increase the obligations of the Alabama Athletic Commission by an undetermined amount to regulate unarmed combat. Any increase in obligations could be offset, wholly or in part, by: (1) license fees imposed for the promotion or holding of unarmed combat events and for participants of unarmed combat events; and (2) administrative fines the commission is authorized, pursuant to the provisions of this bill, to assess and collect in an amount not to exceed $10,000 per violation.
Further, this bill: (1) repeals the current criminal and civil penalties for violation of statutes regarding the commission; and (2) provides a process for filing a complaint with the commission for alleged violations of statutes regarding the commission.
Howard Sanderford, Chair
Boards, Agencies and Commissions
